title: O Darkest Night That Ever Fell
description: O Darkest Night That Ever Fell in Tonic Solfa to ST ANNE, doh is C: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 6 verses and a piano.
about: John Brownlie translated these words from the Greek service books for Hymns from the Morningland (Paisley, 1911).
The book printed the words without tunes. They are in Common Metre (8.6.8.6), and this page sets them to ST ANNE; any other Common Metre tune fits them as well.
underlay: O dark-est night that ev-er fell! Be-fore the sun had set, The light was blot-ted from the heavens, And death, and dark-ness met.

lines: O darkest night that ever fell!
Before the sun had set,
The light was blotted from the heavens,
And death, and darkness met.
For God had turned His face away
From all the sin He bore,
Whom in His love to earth He sent,
To bear our suffering sore.
Ah! darkest night that ever falls
On soul of human race,
When God in anger turns away
The brightness of His face;
Then, sun and moon, and stars are lost,
Amid' our hopeless night;
And all the radiant bliss of life
Is curtained from our sight.
O Christ, Thou art our Light, and Sun,
Our Hope 'mid guilty fears;
No night surrounds Thy presence now,
Nor threatening cloud appears;
And sin and death no longer reign,
Nor day to dark declines,
For, from the Father's face, a light
Of reconcilement shines.

source: John Brownlie, Hymns from the Morningland (1911)
licence: Public domain: John Brownlie died in 1925.
credits: Translated by John Brownlie (1857–1925) from the Greek, public domain, as printed in Hymns from the Morningland; set to ST ANNE by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
